original_value: AbstractResponseNet v.3 is an enhanced version of ResponseNet, a web server that is designed to highlight signaling and regulatory pathways connecting user-defined proteins and genes by using the ResponseNet network optimization approach (http://netbio.bgu.ac.il/respnet). Users run ResponseNet by defining source and target sets of proteins, genes and/or microRNAs, and by specifying a molecular interaction network (interactome). The output of ResponseNet is a sparse, high-probability interactome subnetwork that connects the two sets, thereby revealing additional molecules and interactions that are involved in the studied condition. In recent years, massive efforts were invested in profiling the transcriptomes of human tissues, enabling the inference of human tissue interactomes. ResponseNet v.3 expands ResponseNet2.0 by harnessing ∼11,600 RNA-sequenced human tissue profiles made available by the Genotype-Tissue Expression consortium, to support context-specific analysis of 44 human tissues. Thus, ResponseNet v.3 allows users to illuminate the signaling and regulatory pathways potentially active in the context of a specific tissue, and to compare them with active pathways in other tissues. In the era of precision medicine, such analyses open the door for tissue- and patient-specific analyses of pathways and diseases.

To use ResponseNet, users define source and target sets of proteins, genes, and/or microRNAs and provide a molecular interaction network (interactome). The resulting output is a sparse, high-probability interactome subnetwork that connects the two sets, revealing additional molecules and interactions involved in the condition under study. In recent years, large-scale efforts to profile human tissue transcriptomes have enabled inference of human tissue interactomes. ResponseNet v.3 extends ResponseNet2.0 by using about 11,600 RNA-sequenced human tissue profiles from the Genotype-Tissue Expression consortium to enable context-specific analysis of 44 human tissues. As a result, ResponseNet v.3 helps users highlight signaling and regulatory pathways that may be active in a given tissue and compare them with pathways active in other tissues. In the precision medicine era, such analyses create opportunities for tissue- and patient-specific studies of pathways and diseases.
